name: Anne Beaufour
current_role: Board member of Ipsen (representing family holding Highrock S.à r.l.); director of family holding Mayroy
profile: Granddaughter of Dr. Henri Beaufour, founder of the labs that became French pharma group Ipsen. After her father Albert died in 2000 she and brother Henri controlled ~52-57% of Ipsen via Luxembourg holdings (Mayroy, Highrock, Beech Tree). Switzerland-based; Henri died in Nov 2025, his stake passing to a foundation.
interesting_fact: Ipsen traces back to the Beaufour laboratories founded in 1929 by her grandfather; she holds a geology degree from the University of Paris-Sud (Orsay).
notes: Extremely private; declines comment via Ipsen spokesperson. Brother Henri Beaufour died 28 Nov 2025 - avoid as an outreach topic. Best route is Ipsen corporate communications.

name: Mikheil Lomtadze
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman of the Management Board, Kaspi.kz
profile: Georgian-born Harvard MBA who joined Kaspi via private equity firm Baring Vostok, which invested in the Kazakh bank in 2006. As CEO he rebranded it Kaspi in 2011 and turned it into a super-app combining payments, marketplace and fintech; Kaspi listed in London (2020) and on Nasdaq (2024).
interesting_fact: Before Kaspi he was a partner at Baring Vostok, Russia's largest private equity fund; Kaspi's leadership team pointedly contained no career bankers when it pivoted to technology.
deep_cut_fact: While still a student in Tbilisi he founded his own audit and consulting firm, Georgia Consulting Group Audit (1995), which he later sold.

public_contacts.value: Fintech Leaders interview (Miguel Armaza) - prior podcast appearance

notes: Also spelled Mikhail Lomtadze. Does occasional long-form interviews (McKinsey, Fintech Leaders) - podcast-friendly. Best route: Kaspi IR.

name: Zhou Jianping
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (via Hailan Group), HLA Group Corp. (Shanghai 600398); son Zhou Lichen is chairman
profile: Founder of HLA Group (Heilan Home), one of China's largest menswear makers and retailers. Starting from a small-town photo studio, he took over a collective wool mill in Xinqiao, Jiangyin in 1988 and launched the HLA retail brand around 2002 on a self-service, Uniqlo-style model; he has since handed the chairmanship to his son.
interesting_fact: He never attended university; the money for his first wool-mill venture came from running a photo studio.
deep_cut_fact: In 1984 he opened the first photo studio in his hometown of Xinqiao, Jiangyin; it sat opposite a wool mill, which is how he learned the textile trade before taking over the town's collective mill for 300,000 yuan in 1988.
notes: Very low profile; communicates via HLA's board secretary (Tang Yong). No published personal contact found; route via HLA Group investor relations / SSE roadshow platform.

name: Syed Mokhtar AlBukhary
current_role: Controlling shareholder of MMC Corporation and DRB-HICOM; founder of the Albukhary Foundation
profile: Kedah-born tycoon (b. 1951) who left school before his final exams and began trading and transporting rice in the 1970s. He built a conglomerate spanning ports, logistics, power, construction, autos (DRB-HICOM, Proton stake partner with Geely, 49% of Lotus via Etika), plantations and media (largest Media Prima shareholder).
interesting_fact: His Albukhary Foundation funded the Albukhary Foundation Gallery of the Islamic World at the British Museum (opened 2018) and the wholly charitable Albukhary International University, which offers free degrees to underprivileged students.
deep_cut_fact: His philanthropy predates his fortune: in 1976 he pledged half his salary to 15 underprivileged families and the other half to his mother and siblings.
notes: Famously reclusive; almost never gives interviews. MMC's power arm Malakoff (power generation) is relevant to energy theme. Foundation email is for scholarships, from an older third-party PDF - low value for outreach. Avoid political-donation topics.

name: William Chisholm
current_role: Managing Partner, STG (Symphony Technology Group); Governor and principal owner, Boston Celtics
profile: Massachusetts-raised private equity investor who co-founded Symphony Technology Group with Romesh Wadhwani in 2002 and built it into STG, a software-focused PE firm in Menlo Park. In 2025 he led the group that bought the Boston Celtics for a record $6.1 billion, the highest price ever paid for a US sports team at the time.
interesting_fact: He was on Dartmouth varsity soccer teams that won Ivy League titles in 1988 and 1990, after captaining Brooks School in New England prep soccer.
deep_cut_fact: He left Dartmouth intending to become a teacher, but was drawn by the competitiveness of finance and began his career as an investment banker at PaineWebber before Bain & Co. and venture capital.

public_contacts.value: Prior podcast appearance: Celtics Talk - 'From fan to owner of the Boston Celtics: The Bill Chisholm interview'

notes: Basketballjournal URL slug may differ slightly; Boston Globe paywalled. Route via STG HQ general inbox or Celtics PR. Has done podcast interviews since the purchase.

name: Marcel Erni
current_role: Co-founder and large shareholder, Partners Group (Zug); long-time board member (verify current seat)
profile: Swiss financier who co-founded Partners Group in 1996 with Alfred Gantner and Urs Wietlisbach after stints at McKinsey and Goldman Sachs Zurich. The firm grew from a tiny Ikea-desk office into a global private-markets manager with $185bn+ AUM, listed since 2006; Erni holds ~5%. Chicago Booth MBA '91 and St. Gallen PhD.
interesting_fact: He has described Partners Group's start as 'no money, no clients, no clue'; the founders' original plan was just three partners, one or two deals a year, and time for skiing.
deep_cut_fact: At Chicago Booth he was in Merton Miller's finance class when Miller learned he had won the Nobel Prize, and he loves art: 'If you haven't seen the Seurat (A Sunday on La Grande Jatte) at the Art Institute, you haven't been to Chicago.'
notes: Lowest-profile of the three founders; Partners Group is a big infrastructure investor (incl. data centers/energy), good podcast angle. Could not confirm his 2025-26 board status (search budget exhausted).

name: Jogi Hendra Atmadja
current_role: Founder and President Commissioner (chairman), PT Mayora Indah Tbk
profile: Jakarta-born (1946) University of Indonesia economics graduate who founded Mayora with his siblings in 1977, starting with a biscuit factory in Tangerang. Mayora now owns 50+ brands including Kopiko, Danisa, Beng-Beng, Torabika and Energen, runs 25 factories and exports to 100+ countries; son Andre Sukendra Atmadja is president director.
interesting_fact: Through its Kopiko brand, Mayora is often described as the world's largest coffee-candy maker; Kopiko is exported to more than 100 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Mayora, he started his career as a banker at Bank Central Asia.
notes: Very low public profile, in his late 70s. Deep-cut fact cited via Wikipedia to a Jakarta Post article that was paywalled/403 for me - verify before use. Mayora's published consumer email (consumer@mayora.co.id) is consumer-care only, not a press route.

name: Wang Yun'an
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Guming Holdings (HKEX: 1364), operator of Good Me tea
profile: Born 1986, Wang co-founded Good Me (Guming) with college and high-school friends in 2010, opening a 30 sq m shop in Daxi, Wenling (Zhejiang). He franchised from 2011, focusing on lower-tier cities and building cold-chain supply before stores; Guming now has roughly 10,000 stores and listed in Hong Kong in Feb 2025.
interesting_fact: The first store opened on April 1, 2010 with about RMB 140,000; early daily sales were only RMB 300-500 and the partners debated quitting before it turned around.
deep_cut_fact: A materials-science graduate of Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, he made his first money in college selling quilts and radios, and he personally drew the site-selection and fit-out plans for Guming's first ~150 stores.
notes: Young (b. 1986), first-generation founder - good entrepreneurship story. The press email is listed as Guming's media contact (媒体联系) on its homepage. Briefly worked at a car 4S dealership in Hangzhou before starting Guming.

name: Princess Marie-Chantal
current_role: Founder and creative director, Marie-Chantal (luxury childrenswear brand); Crown Princess of Greece (by marriage)
profile: Born Marie-Chantal Miller in London in 1968, daughter of Robert Warren Miller, co-founder of duty-free giant DFS; the Rich List wealth is shared with her father. Raised in Hong Kong, she married Pavlos, Crown Prince of Greece, in 1995 and in 2000 founded the luxury childrenswear label Marie-Chantal, which opened a London flagship in 2018.
interesting_fact: She met Pavlos in 1993 at a party in New Orleans hosted by Greek shipping magnate Stavros Niarchos; he proposed on a ski lift in Gstaad.
deep_cut_fact: As a high-school student she interned with Andy Warhol, and later studied for a year at the New York Academy of Art.
notes: Wealth source is father Robert Miller (DFS co-founder); listing is a family entry. Best route is via the Marie-Chantal brand. Not an obvious energy/data-center fit; entrepreneurship angle via her own brand.

name: Mathias Doepfner
current_role: CEO and co-owner, Axel Springer SE (Berlin)
profile: Bonn-born journalist (b. 1963) who rose from FAZ music critic to editor-in-chief of Die Welt, then Axel Springer CEO in 2002. He led its digital transformation (Business Insider, Politico) and in 2020 Friede Springer gave/sold him ~22% plus her voting rights; after a 2025 restructuring he and Springer hold ~95% of the media business.
interesting_fact: He started his career in 1982, aged 19, as a music critic for a Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung supplement and later earned a PhD in musicology; he is also a noted art collector.
deep_cut_fact: In autumn 2010 he was a visiting professor at the University of Cambridge (CRASSH), giving three lectures titled 'Freedom and the Digital Revolution' that framed digitization as the fourth great cultural revolution.
notes: High-profile, outspoken; owns Politico and Business Insider, so a US-media angle works. Politically polarizing recently (Politico staff letter 2026) - steer clear in outreach. Route via Axel Springer corporate communications.

name: Xia Yu
current_role: Founder, Chairwoman, President and CEO, Akeso Inc. (HKEX: 9926); director, Summit Therapeutics (Nasdaq: SMMT)
profile: Gansu-born scientist (Michelle Xia) with a Newcastle University PhD who did cancer research in the US and worked at Bayer, PDL BioPharma and Crown Bioscience before co-founding Akeso in Zhongshan in 2012 with under $3m. Akeso's bispecific antibody ivonescimab beat Merck's Keytruda in a 2024 China trial; partner Summit licensed it for the West.
interesting_fact: Named to TIME100 Health in 2025; Akeso's ivonescimab result versus Keytruda was hailed as a watershed moment for Chinese biotech.
deep_cut_fact: Akeso is named after Aceso, the Greek goddess of healing; at its founding the co-founders drew no salaries and hired researchers with only undergraduate degrees.
notes: Goes by Michelle Xia in English. Deep-cut fact sourced via Wikipedia citing WSJ (Apr 2025). Strong founder story; has done Western media (WSJ, Forbes, BioSpace).
